summary: Strengthen clarity, structure, and executive impact with practical writing exercises, revision tools, and AI-assisted drafting methods.
lede: Workplace writing helps professionals turn information into clear documents that support decisions and action. For people who write regularly, this course develops practical ways to plan and revise emails, reports, proposals, and other documents for specific readers. Learners practice audience analysis, concise structure and tone, executive summaries, evidence selection, and editing, with an introduction to AI-assisted drafting and collaborative review.
audienceIntro: This advanced course is built for professionals who already write regularly and now need stronger control over structure, tone, evidence, and revision. It fits roles where writing quality affects approvals, client confidence, internal coordination, and leadership communication.
prerequisites: Participants should already write routine workplace emails, memos, reports, or proposals and be ready to refine them for executive, client, or cross-functional use. A working knowledge of standard office documents is helpful; no coding or technical software setup is required. Access to a laptop for drafting exercises is recommended, and learners should be prepared to bring one real document or document brief from their work context for revision practice. Advanced concepts such as AI-assisted drafting and collaborative editing are taught at an operational application level, not as technical engineering.
